To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) RMS-envelope matching over the entire space-charge-dominated regime of beam intensities is possible with UMER, (b) the high density of UMER quadrupoles is the key factor in achieving this result, (c) the high density also makes the hard-edge model of the magnets a necessity, and (d) the simple general expressions for the envelope matching solutions, valid in the uniform focusing approximation, are a very good approximation to the actual matching solutions.

(1) RMS-envelope matching of electron beams in a fixed lattice can be done over a wide range of beam intensites, and (2) the results of matching can be compared with the predictions from the simple uniform-focusing approximation.

(1) the envelope-matching calculations are accurate, (2) the envelope-mismatching is small (less than 1%), (3) the matching solutions depend on the source parameters, and (4) the matching solutions are robust under realistic operating conditions
In summary, our research is concerned with
the practical aspects of the beam envelope-matching problem for electron beams in periodic lattices, and with the development of accurate hard-edge models for the UMER magnets.
the practical aspects of envelope matching in a periodic focusing channel.
the design and optimization of the UMER FODO lattice for beam transport and matching, including the effects of space charge and nonlinear fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the particular UMER lattice, the envelope matching calculations are in good agreement with experiment.
envelope matching is a powerful tool for beam manipulation and control in a periodic lattice, and that it is a necessary step in any beam optics calculation or simulation.
the matching of beams with extreme space charge is a very practical and important tool in the design of high intensity electron storage rings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the UMER FODO lattice is very well matched for all practical beam currents, and that matching is robust with respect to small changes in beam parameters.
the UMER FODO lattice is very well matched for a broad range of current levels, from zero current to the extreme space-charge limit.
, in principle, the RMS matching procedure is a powerful technique for matching beams over a wide range of intensities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the envelope matching problem for electron beams in periodic focusing systems can be solved accurately and efficiently, even in the case of extreme space-charge effects.
envelope matching can be done with a reasonable degree of precision, over a very broad range of beam currents and lattice strengths, without the need to change the strength of the external focusing.
envelope matching can be a powerful tool for the optimization of beam transport in high-intensity accelerators.
